verdict.rationale: Semgrep's own CLI engine installs locally and scans code on your machine or build environment without an account, and by default code is not uploaded. That covers self-running the core scanner. However, the evidence shows the AppSec Platform (triage, findings API, CI result handling) as a Semgrep-hosted web app, and a community member notes Supply Chain is not open source and may need a service. missing for 10: documented self-hosted deployment of the AppSec Platform/web app, evidence that Pro features (cross-file analysis, Secrets, Supply Chain) run fully offline, explicit open-source licensing details for the core engine.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Semgrep analyzes code locally on your computer or in your build environment: by default, code is never upload
semgrep scan - This is the recommended command for scanning local codebases or scanning a project when you don't have a Semgrep account
You do **not** need to be logged in to run a scan.
You can run local Semgrep CLI scans with the Semgrep command-line tool.
